requirements.title: An input/output error condition makes the file position indeterminate
requirements.definition: If an error condition occurs during execution of an input/output statement, the position of the file becomes indeterminate.

pending.io-error-file-position-indeterminate: No portable oracle may read a specific file position after an I/O error; future error-condition tests close or reestablish the connection before observing subsequent data.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, named intrinsic status values where the standard names them, branch-target execution, or unchanged sentinel values where the source requires no definition. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific nonzero IOSTAT numbers are not asserted.

requirements.title: Unhandled input/output errors initiate error termination
requirements.definition: An I/O error in a statement containing neither ERR= nor IOSTAT= initiates error termination.

pending.io-error-without-err-or-iostat-terminate: In a subprocess fixture, first establish a nonexistent file name with INQUIRE(FILE=..., EXIST=.false.), then OPEN it with STATUS="OLD" and neither ERR= nor IOSTAT=; assert abnormal termination rather than an exact message or status code.

requirements.title: Handled input/output errors terminate list processing and define status specifiers
requirements.definition: When an I/O error occurs and ERR= or IOSTAT= is present, input/output-list processing terminates; IOSTAT=, IOMSG=, and READ SIZE= specifiers that appear become defined as specified by their owning rules.

pending.handled-error-list-processing-terminates: Use a guarded known input error after a first nondefault input item and before a later item; assert only the reported error status and avoid relying on later item values, which may be undefined.
pending.handled-error-iostat-defined: Initialize IOSTAT to zero, provoke a guarded STATUS="OLD" open error with IOSTAT= present, and assert a positive nonzero status without comparing exact values.
pending.handled-error-iomsg-defined: No portable oracle compares IOMSG text or proves assignment changed the previous value; future tests may require only that use of IOMSG does not alter the portable IOSTAT/ERR behavior.
pending.handled-error-read-size-defined: For a future nonadvancing READ error case with SIZE= initialized to a negative sentinel, assert only the value specified by 12.6.2.16 once that SIZE= rule is registered for the chosen transfer.

requirements.title: Handled input/output errors make transfer do-variables and READ input items undefined
requirements.definition: For a data transfer statement or wait operation error, do-variables in the initiating statement become undefined; for READ-initiated errors, input items or namelist group objects in the initiating statement become undefined.

pending.handled-error-do-variables-undefined: No portable oracle may inspect an undefined do-variable after the error; future tests avoid using it after provoking the condition.
pending.handled-error-read-items-undefined: No portable oracle may inspect input items or namelist objects that the source makes undefined after a READ error; future tests reinitialize them before further checks.

requirements.title: ERR= branches on handled input/output errors
requirements.definition: If an ERR= specifier appears for a handled I/O error, execution branches to the statement with the specified label.

pending.handled-error-err-branch: Initialize a branch marker to a nonmatching sentinel, provoke a guarded STATUS="OLD" open error with ERR= and IOSTAT=, set the marker only at the ERR target, and assert the marker and positive IOSTAT without comparing exact status.

accounting.rationale: Error condition effect on file position.
Compound handled/unhandled error effects are split into termination, status, undefinedness, and branch fine units.
Handled error list termination and status specifier effects.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.10.3-12.12: IOLENGTH, error, end-of-record and end-of-file conditions, IOSTAT=, IOMSG=, and restrictions on I/O statements (batch166). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer, accepted with no findings. IOLENGTH's exact count is latitude but its direct-access RECL= suitability is planned; END=/EOR= conditions, IOSTAT_END and IOSTAT_EOR distinctness, zero on success and positive errors are planned portably; IOMSG unchanged on success is planned with a sentinel while condition-message text is never compared. Source accounting only.
